review_status: draft v1 - hardbottom and solution hole profile

profile.diet: Crabs, lobsters, squids, and bottom fishes
profile.behavior: Excavates solution holes and crevice habitats on low-relief hardbottom limestone plains.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, favorable for red grouper.
factors.value_notes: A southeastern Gulf study reports that sea-surface temperature influences red grouper abundance and that thermal relationships differ between juveniles and adults. The Gulf States Marine Fisheries Commission life-history table reports juvenile occurrence at 16.1–31.2 °C and larval optimum estimates of 27.4–28.5 °C. These are stage-specific and regional observations, not a validated adult South Florida SST preference curve; they do not establish the configured 18–28 °C range or 21–25 °C ideal.

factors.reason_template: Bottom is {value}, where red grouper excavate solution holes.
factors.value_notes: NOAA and BOEM describe adults associated with rocky limestone reefs, hardbottom, ledges, crevices, caverns, and wrecks. A NOAA Florida Bay study documents use and excavation of shallow limestone solution holes. This supports the broad hardbottom/reef/ledge categories but does not calibrate their relative numeric scores.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in prime hardbottom depth zone.
factors.value_notes: NOAA describes common shallow-water habitat around 3–18 m; BOEM reports a broad 3–200 m occurrence range with many fish at 30–120 m; the Gulf States life-history table describes juvenile habitat from very shallow water to about 50 m. The configured 10–120 m range and 20–60 m ideal overlap these observations but collapse strong life-stage and habitat-depth differences. Depth is an active gate.

text.dusk: It is dusk, a low-light time when fish feed actively.
